cue: Mostly blue-green and dim, with little colour and soft detail, as a whale or seal sees it.

cpd.note: the middle of the cetacean and seal sharpness records, with the app's pick of 3.5

gain.note: the brightening is the app's pick; the records show a reflecting layer but give no dim-light ratio

BEE_OR_MONO.note: a two-channel reading that stands in for the records, which show only one cone class

rows: Most of these animals have one kind of cone, so they see little or no colour. Their picture is mostly in shades of blue-green and grey.
A bottlenose dolphin, a Bryde's whale and a harbour seal resolve detail to a rough fraction of a person's. We soften the picture to about 3.5 cycles per degree.
Cetaceans and seals have a reflecting layer behind the retina, so dim light is brightened a little. The amount of brightening is the app's own choice.
The colour mapping, the blur and the brightness are the app's own choices. They lean on the records above but are not read from any one animal.
Some settings in this view are the app's own choices, because no measurement gives them. They are set to give a fair picture of the animal and can be tuned by hand.
